{"agent_version": "0.14.0", "task": "Implement `crc.py` in pure Python (standard library only; the suite blocks
`zlib` and `binascii`) so that `python -m pytest tests -q` passes.

  0xEDB88320 reflected), the same function as `zlib.crc32`. The suite holds
  it to the published check values.

same length, `crc32(a ^ b) == crc32(a) ^ crc32(b)` (bytewise xor). Any
correct implementation must satisfy every test.

    suite-green  python -m pytest tests -q passes with all 13 tests (1 check-values, 1 range, 10 xor seeds, 1 no-zlib) and nothing skipped or xfailed.

    bytes-like-input  crc32 accepts bytes, bytearray and memoryview with identical results and raises TypeError for str, as zlib.crc32 does.
    throughput  The 256-entry table is built once at import, and checksumming 1 MiB takes under 1 s on CPython 3.13 on this machine.
    cli  python -m crc FILE... prints '<crc as 8 lowercase hex digits>  <path>' for each file in order, reads stdin when there are no args or '-', and reports unreadable files on stderr, continues, and exits 1.
